guarantees.claim: For each (i,j,k) within generator bounds, ecc_errs[i][j][k] is assigned 1 if the corresponding SECDED decoder detects any error (correctable or uncorrectable) on {key_state_ecc_q[i][j][k], key_state_q[i][j][k]}, else 0.

assumptions.claim: The concatenated input {key_state_ecc_q[i][j][k], key_state_q[i][j][k]} is a valid SECDED-encoded codeword for each i,j,k.
assumptions.cond: when ECC checking is meaningful for key integrity
assumptions.risk: If the data is not properly encoded, ecc_errs may spuriously indicate errors, leading to false error handling, potential key invalidation, or denial of service.

assumptions.claim: Parameters CDIs, Shares, EccWords match the declared dimensions of the key_state_ecc_q and key_state_q arrays.
assumptions.risk: Mismatch would cause out-of-bounds array access, synthesis errors, or undefined behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: SEC-DED corrected data_o and syndrome_o are unconnected; only the error flag is captured. Key material stored in key_state_q may be used directly even when ecc_errs indicates an error, without correction or wipe.
uncertain_points.risk: If corrupted or uncorrectable key data is used, it could lead to cryptographic failures, secret leakage, or security bypass.

uncertain_points.claim: ecc_errs reduces 2-bit decoder error output (correctable/uncorrectable) to a single bit via reduction OR. The design intent for handling different error types is unclear.
uncertain_points.cond: when SECDED decoder signals a correctable vs uncorrectable error
uncertain_points.risk: Loss of information may prevent appropriate responses (e.g., silent correction vs. alert) leading to insufficient error handling.
